Classification guard: the single authored edge asserts association only (etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, hypothesizedOnly:true). It records that chronic inguinal/groin pain after open hernia repair is attributed to ilioinguinal and iliohypogastric nerve injury or entrapment and that nerve-directed treatment relieves that pain in condition-specific series, not that this neuralgia caused chronic pain in any individual; the located evidence includes a six-trial randomized meta-analysis that found no reduction in chronic groin pain when the ilioinguinal nerve was divided, so the mechanism is not asserted at causation strength and an individual claim requires documented nerve injury or entrapment, pain characterization with chronology, and exclusion of the competing causes listed on the edge.

Sibling-consistency guard: the catalog's other peripheral neuralgia identities author single bounded edges (genitofemoral-nerve-neuralgia -> unexplained-chronic-pain; auriculotemporal-neuralgia -> trigeminal-neuralgia), and this batch adds the iliohypogastric/ilioinguinal window on its own nerve-specific primary; no edge is authored to chronic-pelvic-pain-syndrome (wrong-identity guard, as recorded on the genitofemoral sibling), to scars, or to the hernia-repair residuals identities, because those windows belong to their own primaries.

Duplicate-scope guard: the unexplained-chronic-pain identity already receives ten incoming windows (episcleritis, erythromelalgia, femoral-neuropathy, flexor-hallucis-longus-tendinitis, genitofemoral-nerve-neuralgia, glomus-tumor, guillain-barre-syndrome, greater-trochanteric-pain-syndrome, hallux-valgus, hammertoe), none of which is an inguinal nerve-entrapment window, so this batch adds the iliohypogastric/ilioinguinal window on its own nerve-specific evidence.
governanceNotes: D1 batch 48 (2026-09-24): one bounded association edge authored - iliohypogastric/ilioinguinal nerve neuralgia to unexplained-chronic-pain (rank 1), ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, hypothesizedOnly:true, and mechanismCategory MECHANICAL_OR_COMPRESSIVE (suture entrapment, mesh fibrosis, partial division, crushing, and diathermy injury of the inguinal nerves during open repair). The proposition rests on the Thomassen 2013 series of 43 patients treated with ilioinguinal/iliohypogastric nerve blocks for chronic inguinal post-herniorrhaphy pain, in which 38 patients reported outcomes and 21 (55.3%) no longer reported DN4-defined neuropathic pain, with the authors concluding that these blocks can be effective to treat chronic inguinal pain after groin surgery and should be considered before neurectomy, and on the Deepika 2026 prospective observational study of 31 patients per arm, which reports chronic postoperative discomfort in 0.7-36.7% of open inguinal hernioplasty patients, enumerates the mechanisms of ilioinguinal injury during elective repair (suture entrapment, partial division, crushing, and diathermy), and finds that prophylactic ilioinguinal neurectomy significantly reduced groin discomfort and persistent pain to six months. The edge is not raised to causation: the located series are single-centre treatment cohorts without randomization for the block cohort, the outcome measures mix nociceptive and neuropathic pain, and the randomized evidence on the same mechanism is mixed.

Counter-evidence screen recorded 2026-09-24: the Hsu 2012 meta-analysis of six randomized trials with 1,286 patients found no significant difference in chronic groin pain or numbness between preservation and division of the ilioinguinal nerve at one, six, and twelve months, while division significantly increased sensory loss at six months (RR 1.25, 95% CI 1.02-1.53) and twelve months (RR 1.55, 95% CI 1.01-2.37); that study is recorded as screened counter-evidence rather than authored as a source because it does not support the bounded proposition, and it is the reason the mechanism is not asserted at causation strength. Its coexistence with the positive neurectomy and nerve-block series is recorded as unresolved heterogeneity in the located literature rather than as a settled effect direction.

Negative screens recorded 2026-09-24: (i) no chronic-pelvic-pain-syndrome edge - its urological/chronic-prostatitis scope does not fit an inguinal nerve-entrapment source in both sexes (wrong-identity guard, as recorded on the genitofemoral sibling); (ii) no scars, hernia-recurrence, or mesh-complication edge - no condition-specific secondary-outcome data were located and those identities belong to their own primaries (zero-record and duplicate-scope guards); (iii) no erectile-dysfunction, testicular-atrophy, or femoral-neuropathy edge - the located inguinal-nerve literature is about groin pain rather than those outcomes, and the femoral-nerve window belongs to its own identity (zero-record and duplicate-scope guards); (iv) no depressive-disorder or anxiety-disorder edge - no condition-specific psychiatric quantification in inguinal-nerve neuralgia was located (the located Thomassen cohort reports anxiety and depression more often after ultrasound-guided blocks but does not quantify them as outcomes of the neuralgia); (v) no restriction-of-motion or work-limitation edge - no such catalog identities exist (wrong-target guard); (vi) duplicate-scope note: this batch adds the first iliohypogastric/ilioinguinal-primary window to the registry.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Condition-specific clinical series document chronic inguinal pain attributable to ilioinguinal and iliohypogastric nerve injury and its relief with nerve-directed treatment: the Thomassen 2013 series of 43 patients with chronic inguinal post-herniorrhaphy pain treated with ilioinguinal/iliohypogastric nerve blocks found that 21 of 38 respondents (55.3%) no longer reported DN4-defined neuropathic pain and concluded that these blocks can be effective to treat chronic inguinal pain after groin surgery, and the Deepika 2026 prospective study of 31 patients per arm reports chronic postoperative discomfort in 0.7-36.7% of open inguinal hernioplasty patients, enumerates ilioinguinal injury mechanisms (suture entrapment, partial division, crushing, diathermy), and finds significantly reduced groin discomfort and persistent pain to six months after prophylactic ilioinguinal neurectomy - a reproducible co-occurrence association rather than an individual causal nexus.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established: the randomized evidence on the same mechanism is mixed, because a meta-analysis of six trials with 1,286 patients found no difference in chronic groin pain between preservation and division of the ilioinguinal nerve while division increased sensory loss (PMID 22644622), the located treatment series are single-centre and unblinded, and chronic post-herniorrhaphy pain is multifactorial (mesh fixation, recurrence, fibrosis, and pre-existing pain) with nociceptive and neuropathic components that the located outcome measures do not separate; an individual determination therefore requires documented nerve injury or entrapment with chronology relative to the repair, pain characterization, and exclusion of the competing causes listed on this edge.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized mechanical route is described: the ilioinguinal and iliohypogastric nerves run through the operative field of an open inguinal repair and can be injured by suture entrapment, mesh-related fibrosis, partial division, crushing, or diathermy - the mechanisms enumerated in the Deepika 2026 series - producing a painful mononeuropathy that persists after the wound heals, and the pain is attenuated when the affected nerve is blocked or excised, as reported in the Thomassen 2013 block series (55.3% no longer reporting neuropathic pain) and the Deepika 2026 neurectomy arm; the mixed randomized evidence on nerve division and the multifactorial nature of post-herniorrhaphy pain leave individual attribution hypothesized.
causalMechanism.secondaryVector: Mesh fixation technique, tissue fibrosis, hernia recurrence, and pre-existing or centralised pain can each maintain inguinal pain independently of the nerve lesion, and repeated operations and previous groin surgery increase the chance that more than one structure contributes.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The edge asserts an association only: condition-specific series show that chronic inguinal pain after open hernia repair is attributed to ilioinguinal/iliohypogastric nerve injury and that nerve-directed treatment relieves it, but the randomized meta-analysis on the same mechanism found no reduction in chronic groin pain with nerve division, the treatment series are unblinded and single-centre, and post-herniorrhaphy pain is multifactorial, so no at-least-as-likely-as-not probability is asserted and an individual claim requires documented nerve injury or entrapment, pain characterization, chronology relative to the repair, and exclusion of competing causes.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Operative records of the inguinal repair (date, open versus laparoscopic, mesh and fixation technique, whether the nerve was identified, divided, or resected) and of any subsequent reoperation; pain characterization with location, quality, severity, and duration, including a neuropathic screening instrument such as DN4 and the response to ilioinguinal/iliohypogastric nerve block or neurectomy; neurologic examination documenting sensory change or a positive Tinel sign over the inguinal course; imaging or surgical findings of nerve entrapment, meshoma, or fibrosis where obtained; chronology of the pain relative to the repair and to any recurrence or reoperation; assessment of competing causes including hernia recurrence, mesh infection, hip or spine pathology, urological and gynecologic disease, and pre-existing chronic pain conditions; surgical or pain-management assessment of whether the inguinal nerve injury materially contributed to the chronic pain
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Hernia recurrence or meshoma with traction pain
Nociceptive somatic pain from mesh fixation, fibrosis, or the pubic tubercle
Referred pain from hip, lumbar spine, or sacroiliac pathology
Urological or gynecologic causes of chronic groin and pelvic pain
Centralised or pre-existing chronic pain syndrome unrelated to the nerve injury

suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: a 43-patient series treated with ilioinguinal/iliohypogastric nerve blocks for chronic inguinal post-herniorrhaphy pain reported that 55.3% of respondents no longer had DN4-defined neuropathic pain, and a 62-patient prospective study enumerating ilioinguinal injury mechanisms found that prophylactic neurectomy significantly reduced groin discomfort and persistent pain to six months, establishing a reproducible co-occurrence association between inguinal nerve injury and chronic groin pain; the edge is not raised to causation because a six-trial randomized meta-analysis found no difference in chronic groin pain between nerve preservation and division while division increased sensory loss, and because post-herniorrhaphy pain is multifactorial, so the consensus remains NOT_ESTABLISHED with documentation, characterization, chronology, and competing-cause requirements and no probability estimate is asserted.
